standards.title: About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) - The role of the District Court
standards.meta: Netsafe (Approved Agency under the HDCA), last updated 03/11/2025
standards.source_note: Netsafe - About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) (https://netsafe.org.nz/our-work/helpline-services/the-harmful-digital-communications-act), fetched 06/09/2026.
standards.text: Where Netsafe is unable to resolve a complaint or resolve it to the satisfaction of the complainant, it may be possible to seek an order in the District Court. Note that to bring proceedings in the District Court a complaint must first have been made to Netsafe. The District Court has the power to make binding and enforceable orders including: - To take down or disable material. - That the defendant cease or refrain from the conduct concerned. - That the defendant not encourage any other person to engage in similar communications towards the affected individual. - That a correction be published. - That a right of reply be given to the affected individual. - That an apology be published. The Court may also refer the complaint back to Netsafe or dismiss the complaint. It is a criminal offence to fail to comply with an order of the court.

standards.title: About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) - Criminal Offences under the HDCA
standards.meta: Netsafe (Approved Agency under the HDCA), last updated 03/11/2025
standards.source_note: Netsafe - About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) (https://netsafe.org.nz/our-work/helpline-services/the-harmful-digital-communications-act), fetched 06/09/2026.
standards.text: As well as the civil remedies set out above, the HDCA also contains criminal penalties. It is for the Police, rather than Netsafe, to consider whether criminal penalties ought to be pursued.

standards.title: About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) - It is a criminal offence under the HDCA to post a digital communication:
standards.meta: Netsafe (Approved Agency under the HDCA), last updated 03/11/2025
standards.source_note: Netsafe - About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) (https://netsafe.org.nz/our-work/helpline-services/the-harmful-digital-communications-act), fetched 06/09/2026.
standards.text: - With the intention that it cause harm to a victim; or - That is an intimate visual recording of a victim—knowing that the victim has not consented to the posting; orbeing reckless as to whether the victim has consented to the posting. - knowing that the victim has not consented to the posting; or - being reckless as to whether the victim has consented to the posting. The penalty is imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years or a fine not exceeding $50,000 (or in the case of a body corporate, to a fine not exceeding $200,0000).

standards.title: About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) - New Zealand Bill of Rights
standards.meta: Netsafe (Approved Agency under the HDCA), last updated 03/11/2025
standards.source_note: Netsafe - About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) (https://netsafe.org.nz/our-work/helpline-services/the-harmful-digital-communications-act), fetched 06/09/2026.
standards.text: Netsafe (and the District Court) must act consistently with the New Zealand Bill of Rights Act 1990. That Act provides everyone with the right to freedom of expression. However, the right to freedom of expression is not absolute. For example, it does not give someone the right to breach one or more of the communications principles, causing harm to another person. On the other hand, just because someone takes offence or is upset by a digital communication, doesn’t mean that it is a breach of the HDCA.

standards.title: About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) - There may be rights and remedies available under other legislation at the same time as under the HDCA.
standards.meta: Netsafe (Approved Agency under the HDCA), last updated 03/11/2025
standards.source_note: Netsafe - About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) (https://netsafe.org.nz/our-work/helpline-services/the-harmful-digital-communications-act), fetched 06/09/2026.
standards.text: For example, remedies in respect of false allegations might be pursued under the Defamation Act 1992 (as well as or instead of under communications principle 6) and harassment might be pursued under the Harassment Act 1997 (as well as or instead of under communications principle 5). Objectionable content such as child sexual abuse material or terrorist or violent extremist content is dealt with under the Films, Videos and Publications Classification Act 1993. Netsafe works alongside other agencies such as the Classifications Office, the Department of Internal Affairs and the Police in respect of such content.

standards.title: About the Harmful Digital Communications Act (2015) - Some online harms may not be covered by the HDCA.

standards.text: For example, mis or disinformation, financial scams and certain hate speech may not engage the relevant criteria to be considered under the HDCA. Netsafe will still try to help you resolve the issue but the process and our advice may be different.
